### PROCESS LXXVII.
**Tinctura of Tartarized Tartar.**

#### APPARATUS
Take Tartarized Tartar, properly prepared according to Process 75 and dried, then ground into a fine powder. Pour over it, in a tall chemical vial, the purest <term>Alcohol</term> <gloss>spirit</gloss> of wine until it rises four inches above the powder. Then, with the vial stopped only with paper, let them boil together as gently as possible in our wooden furnace for the space of a day and a night. The Alcohol floating on top will be of a golden color, with an aromatic odor and a sharp, hot taste. If this is repeated with new Alcohol in the same manner, a white salt will finally be left at the bottom. The Tinctures are thickened over a gentle fire until a tenth part remains concentrated at the bottom.

#### USE
This serves to demonstrate the part in that Salt which is soluble in Alcohol. The Tincture itself, being aromatic and warming, is prepared for strengthening ulcers and wounds. The remaining salt, which is simpler than before, teaches that the salts themselves can be whitened once the tincture is drawn out by the help of Alcohol.

### PROCESS LXXVIII.
**Dissolution of Regenerated Tartar in Alcohol.**

#### APPARATUS
Take Regenerated Tartar, prepared as neatly as possible beforehand and as safely as can be managed. In a tall chemical glass vial, pour six times as much of the purest Alcohol. Boil it over a gentle fire in our wooden furnace with great prudence. They will combine with one another, and from these will be made a certain uniformly composed substance, once the dregs have settled to the bottom. After they have accurately settled through rest, let the clear, supernatant liquor flow out by a careful tilting of the vessel. If any saline matter not yet dissolved remains, it can be dissolved with the application of fresh Alcohol using the same caution, and thus separated from the dreggy matter. Then, let the prepared liquors be concentrated to half their volume by distilling with a very gentle fire; you will then have the Tincture of this Salt.

#### USE
In this experiment, you see united into one substance the alkali, the oily acid, and the oily spirit of vegetables. From this, the most active principles of plants are freed from the inert earth; yet at the same time they are safe enough, and their sharp bitterness is no longer dangerous. These things, thus united, seem to constitute even the "Lesser Elixir of the Wise" which the Masters of the Ancient Art commended for preserving and restoring health. They say it removes almost all obstacles, 

<column-break/>

penetrates through the vessels, and incites life with a lovely stimulus, so that it heals through <term>diaphoresis</term> <gloss>sweating</gloss>. In Chemistry, it also provides a most effective solvent by which substances are reduced to their smallest, active parts, with their seminal virtue unharmed, so that they can thus be admitted into the inner sanctuaries of the body to restrain and tame every rebellious ailment. Nor is it less praised for the beauty of the effects it performs upon external bodily evils, wounds, ulcers, and tumors. Yet this most healthful remedy should not be denied to the poor, even if it seems ambitious; for it can be prepared immediately by mixing Potash <note>original: "Cineres clavellatos"</note> with fifteen times as much of the sharpest Vinegar, straining, and thickening it. Thus, without the expense of labor or price, a suitable preparation can be made and used. This was known to the ancients in Rome. Pliny, Book 23, in the Preface: "Ash of vine-twigs sprinkled with vinegar is drunk for defects of the spleen."

### PROCESS LXXIX.
**Harvey's Tincture of Salt of Tartar.**

#### APPARATUS
I take the very black alkaline Salt which remained in the glass retort after all the volatile matter was driven out by distillation from Tartar using the highest heat of a sand bath, according to Process 55. This salt, quickly crushed into a powder in a warm iron mortar with a warm pestle and put into a tall glass vial, I pour over with the best common spirits of Wine, so that they float four fingers above. I boil it over a gentle fire in this tall vial, in our wooden furnace, for twenty hours. A thin black liquor will be obtained, with a bitter, aromatic, and <term>lixivious</term> <gloss>alkaline/lathery</gloss> taste. Let this be poured off pure. Thus it can be kept unharmed under its own title in a closed vessel for its intended uses.

#### USE
Common spirit of Wine, consisting of water, acid, and alcohol united, when boiling with the alkali of Tartar (which is still oily), makes a gentler and safer lye. This is because the alkali is tempered by the acid, oil, and alcohol; from which is born a type of medicament and <term>menstruum</term> <gloss>solvent</gloss> that is not ignoble. In Chemistry, when cooked or digested with vegetables, it performs well by beautifully dissolving simple substances. In Surgery, it is a most noble remedy for purifying, cleansing, drying, and consolidating moist, purulent, rotten, foul, and virulent ulcers, and bad habits of the body <note>original: "cacoëthe"</note>, whether they be full of fistulas or winding passages and deep-eating channels; also for consuming those things which grow out with excessive luxuriance, especially if it is mixed skillfully with a little oil.
